faults.quote: Hollis Bay's two largest retail partners have agreed to stock the line in all their stores, provided Hollis Bay pays the shelf fees.
faults.why: The candidate asked about distribution reach, number of stores and turns per store per week. Only the retailer-support line went out. Store count and turns got no word, not even an 'I don't have'.

faults.quote: You've put the break-even at about 5.6 million bags. Before we size volume, how would you judge whether that's a high or low hurdle for this launch?
faults.why: The interviewer restates the candidate's wrong 5.6M break-even, built on the miscalculated $1.40 cost, as the working hurdle. It invites further analysis on it before probing the error.

faults.quote: As I mentioned: Hollis Bay's two largest retail partners have agreed to stock the line in all their stores, provided Hollis Bay pays the shelf fees.
faults.why: An already-released line is repeated as the answer to an explicit ask for store count, which it doesn't answer. There is no 'I don't have the store count'.

faults.quote: Category size and growth for better-for-you snacks in the Northeast and Midwest — that's not something I have.
faults.why: Growth is coarsely answered by the case (why_now, and the prompt says better-for-you snacks are growing quickly), so 'not something I have' is not true for the growth part. That coarse answer was already in front of the candidate.

The candidate stated a want to know who the incumbents are and whether a dominant brand is already in the stores. The competition_general ledger item answers this, but it got no release, refusal or deferral.

faults.quote: Category size and growth for better-for-you snacks in the Northeast and Midwest — that's not something I have.
faults.why: The candidate again asked for the store count for the two partners. It got no word at all, after being met only with a restatement at t12.

faults.quote: Three doubts: conversion, repeat and cannibalization.
faults.why: The candidate stated a want to know whether the 60%/20% conversion rates come from Hollis Bay's own past launches. The survey_reliability ledger item answers this, but it was not released or addressed.

faults.quote: Fewer than 5% of chickpea-snack purchases are expected to replace a bag of Hollis Bay's own chips — small enough to ignore for this decision.
faults.why: The candidate asked whether survey respondents are current chip buyers. The cannibalization line answers the underlying concern but not the respondent-mix question, and there is no 'I don't have' for that part.

faults.quote: What would you do to guard against that?
faults.why: The candidate's last answer had just laid out mitigations: diagnosis, freezing spend, and pull-back thresholds. Asking how to guard against the risk re-asks what was just covered.
